comments.note: MainContentViewModel.cs: The parameterless design-time constructor (retained for backward compat) creates no IDatabaseBackupDialogService, so BackupDatabase RelayCommand will silently no-op if ever called in design-time. Consider adding a guard or XML doc comment to clarify this is intentional.

Program.cs: ObfuscationSettingsViewModel and SettingsViewModel are registered with AddSingleton<T>() generic form which relies on constructor analysis. As SettingsViewModel’s constructor grows, this is fine. If a future refactor adds multiple constructors, switching to explicit factory lambda would make the intent unambiguous.
No observations outside the touched files — all other source code examined is clean and consistent.

summary: Reviewed all four modified files: MainContentView.axaml, MainContentViewModel.cs, Program.cs, MainContentViewModelTests.cs. All 7 acceptance criteria met. No blocking issues found.

comments.note: [documentation-forward] MainContentViewModel.BackupDatabase is not covered by any test — BuildSut() passes backupDialogService: null so the command body is always a no-op in the test suite. A single test such as BackupDatabaseCommand_WhenServiceIsNull_ExecutesWithoutException would provide a regression guard and document the intentional silent no-op behaviour. Add to api-surface.md that BackupDatabase is guarded by a null-check for design-time/test compatibility.

Program.cs: sp.GetService<IDatabaseBackupDialogService>() (non-required) is the correct choice — it returns null when the service is not registered (test containers), matching the IDatabaseBackupDialogService? nullable parameter and the null-guard in BackupDatabase. This is a well-reasoned defensive pattern; no change needed.
No observations outside the touched files — code is clean and consistent.
